rationale: The labels remain O(n²) time and O(n) auxiliary space; this revision corrects assumptions and rationale only. In a merge of two non-empty halves, one half is eventually exhausted by repeated pop(0) calls. The shifts from removing all elements of that half sum to Θ(n²) for the top-level merge regardless of input order, so T(n)=2T(n/2)+Θ(n²)=Θ(n²). Excluding input and returned output, recursion slices and intermediate lists use O(n) peak auxiliary storage. The source docstring says O(n log n), but that claim omits list.pop(0) shifting costs.

The owner approves the proposed complexity labels. The int table has (m+1)(k+1) cells, giving Θ(mk) time and auxiliary space for non-empty strings. Backtracking uses StringBuilder append/reverse in O(m+k), not repeated concatenation. Null or empty input returns before allocating the table. The coarse O(n²) class uses n=max(m,k), with comparable lengths required for a tight Θ(n²) statement.
